I will still do it mostly the way I know, starting from last year and only changing a little. I have 14 mu, and home labor is not too much because some people work outside, so I will not spread myself too thin on crops that need too much hand work. Wheat and maize are my steady crops, so I will keep most land in that wheat-maize rotation, 8 mu total on the same land. The other 6 mu I will split into 3 mu chili and 3 mu cotton, same as the kind of mix that lets me keep grain in hand and still chase some cash income. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a little on fertilizer and lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I will follow what has worked around me: decent base fertilizer, topdressing when the crop is really taking off, and using well water when the field looks dry. Wheat I will feed a bit heavier because it is my base crop. Maize I will also push, because if rain is short I can still use the well. Chili needs more watching, more water, and more spraying, but on only 3 mu I can still manage it. Cotton I will keep in the middle, not the heaviest input, but I will not starve it either. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen neighbors get better stands and better yield, because if I can see it working in nearby fields, I trust it.
